clue.text: Unexpectedly cheap? It's only imitation

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly comes out in a surprising way, so these letters turn up rearranged

parts.note: the possessive-looking apostrophe gives no letter, so this is just I, T and S

explanation.surface: A remark that a cheap-looking item is merely a copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' signals an anagram of CHEAP plus ITS; 'only' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a work that copies the style of another artist or period.

clue.text: Girl admits making gains, being irreligious

indicators.note: the girl's name lets something in, so the other piece goes inside it

parts.note: Pam is a girl's name

indicators.note: making means forming something, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl confesses to profiting from turning away from religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl' could be any name; the right one has to hold an anagram of the remaining letters, and 'admits' says it encloses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Paganism is the holding of heathen beliefs outside the main religions.

clue.text: Lively pair in visually attractive surroundings

indicators.note: the pair goes in the other word, which surrounds it

parts.note: sightly means pleasing to the eye

explanation.surface: A lively couple in pretty surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surroundings' confirms that the attractive word encloses the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly means full of energy, brisk and spirited.

clue.text: The centre of Bury is at last still

indicators.note: the middle letter is now placed at the end, the last position

parts.note: to inter is to bury
the middle letter of the five-letter word for bury is T

explanation.surface: The middle of the town of Bury has finally gone quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town near Manchester, but here it means INTER; its centre letter T moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless, lacking the power to move.

clue.text: Poor performer on imitation bed

parts.note: a ham is a bad, overacting actor
mock means imitation, as in mock leather

explanation.surface: A bad actor lying on a fake bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammock is a hanging bed of canvas or netting.

clue.text: Be established and secure

explanation.surface: An instruction to settle in and make oneself safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom that obtains is one that prevails or holds good, and to obtain something is to get or acquire it.

clue.text: Celebration where the pulses may be stirred?

definitions.text: Celebration where the pulses may be stirred?

parts.words: Celebration where the pulses may be stirred?
parts.note: pulses here are not heartbeats but peas and lentils, stirred in a pot for a feast

explanation.surface: A party so exciting it gets everyone's heart racing.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulses are edible seeds; the party name literally contains a pulse.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanfeast is a jolly celebration or party, originally an employer's annual dinner for workers.

clue.text: A servant buried one with great haste

indicators.note: the one is buried inside the word for servant

parts.note: a man is a manservant
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A servant burying somebody in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Amain is an old word meaning at full speed or with force.

clue.text: It may indicate an upward turn in old age, even

indicators.note: in a down clue an upward turn reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: eld is an archaic word for old age
e'en is a poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: Something that could show a revival in old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an upward turn' reverses ELD plus EEN, giving NEEDLE; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer on a dial or compass shows a reading.

clue.text: Distant body administered university in America

indicators.note: the pieces go in the word for America

parts.note: US is short for United States, America
to run a business is to administer it, so ran

explanation.surface: A remote organisation that ran an American university.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh planet, far out in the solar system.

clue.text: Old American has gone from strikingly beautiful ravine

indicators.note: one thing having gone from another means it has been taken away from that word

parts.note: strikingly beautiful means gorgeous
US is short for United States, so for American

explanation.surface: An old American has left a beautiful canyon.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorge is a narrow steep-sided valley, the same thing as a ravine.

clue.text: Preserve, or ruin, young fellow in West

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil or ruin it

indicators.note: the young fellow is placed inside the word for West

parts.note: Mae West was the American film actress, so West gives her first name MAE
a lad is a young fellow

explanation.surface: A choice between saving or wrecking a young man out in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like a compass point but stands for the actress Mae West; 'or' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus jam, a fruit preserve eaten on toast.

clue.text: Reportedly honour University members — before retirement, it's assumed

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word for honour is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to knight someone is to honour them with a title
gown stands for the members of a university, as in the phrase town and gown

explanation.surface: University staff being honoured just before they retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' looks like leaving work but means going to bed; the garment is assumed, that is put on, before then.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is put on, or assumed, just before going to bed for the night.

clue.text: Football administrators left outside during the big game

indicators.note: these two pieces go outside the word for during, enclosing it

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, which runs English football
in means during, as in 'in the night'

explanation.surface: Football officials left out of the action during the cup final.
explanation.definitionFit: The final is the deciding match of a competition, the biggest game of the tournament.

clue.text: A reversal of fortune for an educational journal

explanation.surface: A school magazine suffering a downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: the TES (Times Educational Supplement, a British teachers' paper) is SET written back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a misfortune that checks progress, and the letters SET put back spell the initials of a teachers' weekly.

clue.text: Sailor caught in absurd act in Southern Region

indicators.note: the sailor and the catch go inside the scrambled letters
absurd means nonsensical, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A seaman caught behaving ridiculously in the southern polar region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like part of the sailor's story but is the cricket abbreviation C; the first 'in' is the container signal and the second is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antarctic is the polar region around the South Pole.

clue.text: Drink prepared by quiet boy

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
Andy is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A drink mixed by a silent lad.
explanation.walkthrough: SHANDY is a British drink of beer mixed with lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is a beverage of beer cut with lemonade or ginger beer.

clue.text: Welshman has lines composed, say, to a country girl

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, so made is heard as a girl

parts.note: made means composed, put together

explanation.surface: A Welshman has written verses to a rural lass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' looks like poetry but means railway lines; 'has' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairymaid is a young woman who milks cows on a farm.

clue.text: Animals found in three rivers, including one in Germany

indicators.note: the rivers include, or contain, the German number

parts.note: R is short for river, and the Dee is a river in Britain, giving three rivers in all
the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
another R, the abbreviation for river
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: Creatures discovered among several rivers, one of them in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Reindeer are Arctic deer, herded in Lapland and pulling Santa's sleigh.

clue.text: It's becoming messy round the Square — orderliness is needed

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the piece for square, enclosing it
the word messy is becoming something else, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing tool, so T can stand for square

explanation.surface: Things getting untidy around the town square call for tidiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' turns MESSY into SYSEM, which goes 'round' T for SYS-T-EM; 'It's' and 'is needed' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is a methodical, organised way of doing things.

clue.text: Noah's son, climbing up without the elephant driver?

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Ham was one of the sons of Noah
out means outside or without

explanation.surface: Noah's son scrambling aboard without the elephant handler.
explanation.definitionFit: A mahout is a person who works with and rides an elephant in South Asia.

clue.text: A good person to journey on horseback, perhaps

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a good person
to ride is to journey on a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: A virtuous traveller who goes about mounted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' because one can sit this way on a fence or chair as well as a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with a leg on each side, as a rider sits a horse.

clue.text: Gas used in projectiles, not in activating launchers

parts.note: ammo is short for ammunition, the projectiles fired

indicators.note: the launchers are the starting letters, the ones that launch each word

explanation.surface: A gas used in missiles, not in the launchers that fire them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launchers' means the first letters of NOT IN ACTIVATING; 'used in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammonia is a pungent colourless compound of nitrogen and hydrogen, a gas.

clue.text: Entanglement of soldiers in large numbers

indicators.note: the soldiers go in the word for large numbers

parts.note: a mass is a great quantity
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers caught up in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a bog, and by extension a confusing tangle.

clue.text: Name in small capitals entered in the sweep

indicators.note: one piece is entered into another, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a sweep is a long oar used to row a large boat
sc is the printers' abbreviation for small capitals

explanation.surface: A name written in small capitals is put into the lottery draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweep' suggests a sweepstake but is a long oar.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar is a man's first name.

clue.text: Singers I interrupted during endlessly tedious work

indicators.note: the letter I breaks in during the other word, sitting inside it
endlessly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a chore is a tedious task

explanation.surface: Singers I interrupted while doing dull work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the E of CHORE to give CHOR, then I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is a group of singers.

clue.text: Like Kipling's peasant's greeting to an old Asian?

parts.note: hi is a casual greeting
a Malayan is someone from Malaya, the old name for part of what is now Malaysia

explanation.surface: How a rustic in a Kipling story might hail an Asian of former times.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's peasants in stories such as 'The Miracle of Purun Bhagat' live in the mountains of northern India; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling set stories among hill people of the great mountain range north of India.

clue.text: Gradual decline of some Scandinavians, say

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken aloud, so it is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Lapps are the people of Lapland in northern Scandinavia

explanation.surface: The slow decline of certain Nordic peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slipping or falling away, a gradual decline in standards.

clue.text: Sporting event restricted by a shock policy change

indicators.note: the sporting event is hemmed in, or restricted, by the other pieces around it

parts.note: a turn is a sudden fright, as in 'you gave me a turn'
a bout is a boxing or wrestling contest

explanation.surface: A sports fixture curtailed by a sudden surprise reversal of plans.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of opinion or policy, from the military drill of turning to face the other way.

clue.text: Difficult stage in plotting graph, as every schoolboy knows

indicators.note: in plotting points to letters lying inside the words graph, as every that are being plotted

explanation.surface: Learning to draw graphs is a tricky stage every pupil goes through.
explanation.definitionFit: Going through a phase means a passing, often troublesome period of development.

clue.text: Smart club in super building

indicators.note: the club letter goes inside the rearranged letters
building means constructing something new, so the letters of super are put together afresh

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for club, the card suit

explanation.surface: A stylish nightclub housed in a superb building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges SUPER into SPRUE, and 'in' puts C inside it for SPRU-C-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means neat and trim in appearance.

clue.text: Sounds like a press timetable

indicators.note: sounds like means the word for timetable is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a calendar is a schedule of dates, a timetable

explanation.surface: A newspaper's schedule that is said to be like the press.
explanation.definitionFit: A calender is a machine with rollers that presses cloth or paper smooth.
